Why sourdough needs time

By Ada Baker

A sourdough starter is a colony of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria, and the slow fermentation is what gives the loaf its flavour.

Rushing the proof with warm water makes a loaf that rises but tastes flat, because the bacteria have not had time to make the acids that carry the taste.

The overnight rule

Most bakers leave the dough in the fridge overnight. Read our cold proof guide for the details.

  • Feed the starter twelve hours before.
  • Mix, rest, fold three times.
